title: postfix ! is accepted in a concise arrow body whose arrow declares a Result channel
notes: specification/failures.mdx, 'Accepted Placements': 'A `!` on a Result operand MUST be accepted if and only if all five hold', condition 1 being that every enclosing node out to the nearest statement or arrow function is one of exactly seven forms. The walk in condition 1 stops at 'the nearest statement OR ARROW FUNCTION'. An arrow function is therefore a STOP, not a rejection: the propagation returns from the arrow, which is the function whose declared channel condition 3 is asking about, and here that arrow spells `Result<string, Missing>`. 07-must-consume/a-concise-arrow-body-returning-a-result-is-a-return pins the must-consume half of the same reading — `=> e` is a `return`. This case pins the placement half, and it is deliberately the spelled-contract spelling so that condition 3 is satisfied by an authored annotation rather than by inference. RETIRED XFAIL (go): the fork reported SMITHERS1204@11:58 and refused this program, because `safeUnwrapPlacement` answered `false` whenever the placement walk stopped at an arrow function — "a concise arrow body has no statement list to hoist a guard into", which is true of the AUTHORED form and irrelevant to the lowered one. The fix is the lowering feature the marker asked for, not a table entry: `lowerConciseBody` now SYNTHESISES the block body when a propagation point in the body hoisted a guard, so `=> lookup(key)!` lowers to `=> { const t = lookup(key); if (!t.ok) return t; return new Ok(t.value) }`. The arrow's own declared channel stays the channel the early return exits through, which is what condition 3 asks about. The placement rule was ALSO factored while it was open: membership of `hoistableStatements` used to be re-tested by each of `safeUnwrapPlacement`'s two callers, and now lives inside it, so the two cannot drift apart about what a safe placement is. MEASURED, not assumed: the fork's three hoisting sites are `lowerExpect`, `lowerPropagation` and `matchScrutinee`; the first two share `safeUnwrapPlacement` and both are fixed by the one seam, and the third is gated by `canHoist` instead and was probed separately — a non-identifier `.match` receiver in a concise arrow body runs and prints identically on both backends, so it was not a member of this defect.
